summary: Task 8 (commit 72b4e03) wires i18n into app.vue and the two layouts. Diff is presentation-only: useLocaleHead({ seo: true }) + useHead in app.vue, t()-driven labels and NuxtLinkLocale in default.vue, LangSwitcher placement in auth.vue, and a key-flattening edit to uk/en locale JSON. No new dependencies, no new endpoints, no auth boundary changes, no user-controlled inputs introduced. Focus areas verified: (1) hreflang alternates emitted by useLocaleHead are derived from route name/params, not route.query — orchestrator's SSR curl capture confirms <link rel="alternate" href="/auth/login" hreflang="uk"> with no ?token= leakage; defense-in-depth from Task 2 already applies X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow and Referrer-Policy: no-referrer to /auth/** and /{locale}/auth/**. (2) The SSR head fragments contain only htmlAttrs.lang/dir, og:locale meta, and rel=alternate links — no user data, no tokens, no auth state. (3) Logout calls navigateTo(localePath('/auth/login')) where the argument is a hardcoded literal — no open-redirect surface. (4) LangSwitcher placement in auth.vue exposes only locale-switching UI pre-login (component audited in Task 6); no sensitive data is referenced. (5) All translated strings render via Vue mustache binding which HTML-escapes by default; locale dictionaries are committed JSON, not user input — no XSS surface. (6) No hardcoded secrets in diff. OWASP Top 10 sweep over the diff yields no applicable findings. Verdict: OK.
